finding.title: The code uses scanf to read an integer from the user. If the user inputs a value that is too large to fit in an int, it can lead to a buffer overflow.
The code does not handle errors from sendto and recvfrom functions, which can lead to undefined behavior if these functions fail.
The code does not validate the input received from the server, which could lead to unexpected behavior if the server sends invalid data.
The memset function is used to clear the server_addr structure, but it should be cleared with sizeof(server_addr) instead of sizeof(int).

scan_orig.message: Avoid using 'scanf()'. This function, when used improperly, does not consider buffer boundaries and can lead to buffer overflows. Use 'fgets()' instead for reading input.

scan_patch.message: Avoid using 'scanf()'. This function, when used improperly, does not consider buffer boundaries and can lead to buffer overflows. Use 'fgets()' instead for reading input.
